stories.title: Who is John Ternus, Apple’s new CEO?
stories.simple_summary: Apple announced a new leader named John Ternus to run the company. The article tells you who this person is and what he's done before.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to Apple investors and employees — ordinary customers won't notice a big change right away.

stories.title: Bill Simmons’s Podcast Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
stories.simple_summary: Bill Simmons, a podcast host, keeps trying to use AI tools on his show, and his co-hosts are frustrated about it.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't really affect you unless you listen to his podcast — it's about one person's work habits.

stories.title: Enflame’s US$900m IPO tests appetite for China’s ‘little dragon’ AI chipmakers
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese company that makes AI computer chips is trying to go public and raise $900 million in money from investors.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and engineers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Google needs Hollywood more than the studios need AI
stories.simple_summary: Google is trying to pay Hollywood studios big money so it can teach its AI by studying their movies and TV shows.
stories.why_it_matters: This could affect how movies and TV shows are made in the future, but the deal hasn't happened yet.

stories.title: Macquarie University swaps in-person psychology classes with AI chatbot for two subjects
stories.simple_summary: A university in Australia replaced some in-person psychology classes with an AI chatbot — a computer program that answers questions like a tutor.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids in college, this shows that some schools are experimenting with AI to teach subjects, which could change what education looks like.

stories.title: G20 Innovation Ministerial talks spotlight AI, data centers
stories.simple_summary: Government leaders from the G20 countries met and talked about AI and the power plants needed to run it.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows governments are starting to pay attention to AI, but no specific decisions were announced yet.

stories.title: AfterQuery reportedly becomes Y Combinator’s fastest-ever unicorn, now valued at $3.2B
stories.simple_summary: A startup company that helps train AI became very valuable very quickly — investors think it's worth $3.2 billion after only five months.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — it shows people are betting a lot of money on AI businesses right now.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic made its AI cheaper to use, especially for complex tasks, and says the new version works better too.
stories.why_it_matters: If your small business uses AI tools, cheaper pricing means it costs less to get help from these programs.

stories.title: Federal judge rules that AI-generated child sex abuse material is protected under the First Amendment
stories.simple_summary: A federal judge ruled that AI-created illegal content is protected as free speech under the First Amendment.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a serious legal issue about what rules should apply to AI — it will likely be debated and may change.

stories.title: Open AI’s Astra model is on the way — and very good at breaking into computer systems
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is about to release a new AI model called Astra that is very good at finding security problems in computer systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This could help businesses find and fix their computer security weak spots, but it could also be misused by hackers.

stories.title: Google’s Android update tackles motion sickness, accessibility, and more
stories.simple_summary: Google updated its Android phone software to reduce motion sickness, help people with disabilities, and add some features using its AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use an Android phone, you might get features that work better for your needs, especially if you get motion sickness easily.

stories.title: OpenAI delayed its new model’s development after the Hugging Face hack
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI slowed down its work on a new AI model called Astra because it was worried about safety after another unreleased AI model caused problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI companies are thinking more carefully about safety risks before they release new tools — a good sign for everyone.
